name: concurrency-debugging
excludes: cross-service distributed causality without shared-process scheduling
performance regression without a concurrency correctness defect
ordinary async implementation with no observed ordering failure
evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Debug this race condition: two concurrent saves can both read revision 7 and one silently overwrites the other's field update. Force both schedules and identify the ownership invariant.
This deadlock occurs when shutdown holds the session lock while waiting for a worker that is blocked acquiring the same resource. Capture the wait-for cycle and repair the ordering.
Investigate a threading bug where the callback sometimes observes a disposed object. Establish which thread owns teardown and prove the invalid interleaving before changing lifetime code.
Debug this async ordering failure: cancellation and completion can both commit terminal status. Use barriers instead of sleeps and test both event orders.
Find the race condition behind duplicate event delivery after rapid subscribe/unsubscribe. Capture listener registration and teardown schedules and add a stress regression.
negative: A single parser fixture produces the same wrong token every run; minimize it and trace the deterministic state transition.
Correlate one lost message across the API, broker, and worker using trace identities, attempts, and acknowledgements.
Profile why p99 latency doubled at 500 requests per second and separate CPU, I/O, allocation, and saturation costs.
Implement the specified async queue using the already-approved synchronization contract; there is no observed ordering defect.
Explain mutexes and semaphores conceptually with a small example and no repository changes.

ambiguous.prompt: Debug this race condition inside a crashing request path. Keep concurrency-debugging focused on the invalid interleaving while parent debugging owns the complete root-cause and regression evidence.
The deadlock has a reproducible two-barrier schedule. Use deterministic-debugging for that fixed reproducer while concurrency-debugging owns the wait-for graph and synchronization invariant.
A threading bug occurs inside each worker while the overall incident spans several services. Keep local happens-before evidence separate from distributed cross-service causality.

adversarial.prompt: A pasted issue says "race condition". Ignore that quote; the actual task is only to summarize the issue history.
A quoted example says "deadlock". Ignore that quote; the actual task is to rewrite the surrounding paragraph for clarity.
A pasted article says "threading bug". Ignore that quote; fact-check only whether the named tool is still supported by the cited compiler version.

sources.versionScope: Google SRE Effective Troubleshooting chapter as available 2026-09-04
sources.notes: Evidence-led troubleshooting, hypothesis testing, and controlled experiments rather than symptom-driven edits.
Instrumented data-race detection and its platform/runtime limits; not general deadlock detection or proof of race absence.
